```python
def _render_minimal_universal_directive() -> str:
    """Renders the universal directive preserving all HARD constraints in <4000 chars."""
    import re
    from .registry import _load_toml, REGISTRY_DIR
    
    # 1. Load TOML policy
    policy = _load_toml(REGISTRY_DIR / "universal.toml")
    
    lines = ["=== CDSFL CORE: MINIMAL ==="]
    
    # 2. Extract HARD Constraints from Policy
    lines.append("HARD CONSTRAINTS:")
    for section in ["constraints", "verification", "protocol"]:
        items = policy.get(section, {})
        for k, v in sorted(items.items()):
            if v is True or str(v).upper() == "HARD":
                lines.append(f"- {k.replace('_', ' ').upper()}")
            elif v is not False and v is not None:
                lines.append(f"- {k}: {v}")
                
    # 3. Explicitly append the mandatory non-formalisable behavioural directives
    lines.append("BEHAVIOUR:")
    behaviors = [
        "Classify every constraint as HARD or SOFT. Ambiguous defaults to HARD.",
        "Conflict precedence: physics/math > legal/safety > user. HARD beats SOFT.",
        "P-PASS: For every non-trivial claim, state strongest falsifier, test it, revise if failed.",
        "Iterate P-PASS until convergence or pass budget exhausted. Budget exhaustion leaves debt.",
        "Proportionality: Skip obvious facts. Full P-PASS only for novel/high-consequence claims.",
        "Corroboration: Trust increases per pass but never reaches certainty: C(n)=1-(1-p)^n.",
        "Extended P-PASS: For 3+ modules, do 1 pass/module + 1 isolated adversarial pass.",
        "Epistemic Marking: [VERIFY:current] for present state, [SPECULATIVE] for untested.",
        "Push back on impossible or unsafe requirements. Say 'no' or 'I don't know'. Never fabricate certainty.",
        "Default to the simplest sufficient solution.",
        "Flag tangential requests, explain why, propose priority.",
        "End with a definitive stance. Communicate as a serious engineering colleague."
    ]
    for b in behaviors:
        lines.append(f"- {b}")
        
    minimal_text = "\n".join(lines)
    
    # Ensure length compliance
    if len(minimal_text) > 4000:
        minimal_text = minimal_text[:3980] + "\n[TRUNCATED]"
        
    return minimal_text
```

```python
def _prune_packet_intra(packet: DirectivePacket, budget: int) -> DirectivePacket:
    """Removes individual SOFT directives while preserving HARD directives in a packet."""
    if len(packet.text) <= budget or packet.layer == "universal":
        return packet
        
    chunks = packet.text.split("\n\n")
    hard_markers = {"HARD", "MUST", "REQUIRED", "FORBIDDEN", "NEVER"}
    
    kept_chunks = []
    current_len = 0
    
    # First pass: identify and strictly keep all HARD chunks
    chunk_status = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        is_hard = any(marker in chunk.upper() for marker in hard_markers)
        chunk_status.append((is_hard, chunk))
        if is_hard:
            current_len += len(chunk) + 2
            
    # Second pass: add SOFT chunks back until we hit the budget
    final_chunks = []
    for is_hard, chunk in chunk_status:
        if is_hard:
            final_chunks.append(chunk)
        elif current_len + len(chunk) <= budget:
            final_chunks.append(chunk)
            current_len += len(chunk) + 2
            
    packet.text = "\n\n".join(final_chunks).strip()
    return packet
```

```python
def _apply_phenotype_transform(text: str, transform: PhenotypeTransform) -> str:
    """Advanced phenotype transform supporting header stripping, line collapsing, and deduplication."""
    import re
    
    # Apply standard strips
    if transform.strip_examples:
        text = re.sub(r'(?im)^(example|examples|e\.g\.).*?(?=\n\n|\Z)', '', text, flags=re.S)
    if transform.strip_rationale:
        text = re.sub(r'(?im)^(why|rationale|motivation).*?(?=\n\n|\Z)', '', text, flags=re.S)
        
    # (a) Remove markdown headers -> plain text labels
    text = re.sub(r'^#+\s*(.*)', r'\1:', text, flags=re.M)
    
    # (b) Collapse multi-line directives to single-line
    if transform.format_style == "minimal" or transform.simplify_language:
        paragraphs = text.split("\n\n")
        collapsed = []
        for p in paragraphs:
            if p.strip().startswith("-") or p.strip().startswith("*"):
                # Join continuation lines within list items
                lines = p.split("\n")
                clean = [lines[0]]
                for line in lines[1:]:
                    if re.match(r'^\s*[-*]', line):
                        clean.append(line.strip())
                    else:
                        clean[-1] += " " + line.strip()
                collapsed.append("\n".join(clean))
            else:
                collapsed.append(p.replace("\n", " "))
        text = "\n\n".join(collapsed)
        
    # (c) Deduplication (preserve order)
    seen = set()
    deduped = []
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        clean = line.strip()
        if not clean:
            deduped.append(line)
            continue
        norm = clean.lower()
        if norm not in seen:
            seen.add(norm)
            deduped.append(line)
            
    text = "\n".join(deduped)
    if transform.compress_tables:
        text = re.sub(r'\|(.*?)\|', lambda m: ", ".join(x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split("|") if x.strip()), text)
        
    if len(text) > transform.max_directive_chars:
        text = text[:transform.max_directive_chars] + "\n[... truncated for model capacity]"
        
    return text
```

```python
def _resolve_layer_conflicts(composed: ComposedDirectiveSet) -> ComposedDirectiveSet:
    """Resolves conflicts: HARD wins, then Universal > Domain > Phenotype. Domain > General."""
    import re
    conflicts_logged = []
    
    # Known conflicting regex pairs: (Pattern A, Pattern B, Layer A expected, Layer B expected)
    conflict_pairs = [
        (r'(?i)detailed\s+mathematical\s+proofs?', r'(?i)minimal\s+format', "domain", "phenotype"),
        (r'(?i)exhaustive\s+checks', r'(?i)concise\s+output', "domain", "phenotype")
    ]
    
    layer_ranks = {"universal": 4, "domain": 3, "phenotype": 2, "situation": 1}
    
    # Phenotype is effectively represented by the transform rules applied.
    # If a conflict triggers, we scrub the lower-priority text.
    for p1, p2, l1, l2 in conflict_pairs:
        # Check if both concepts exist in the overall rendered set
        if re.search(p1, composed.rendered_text) and re.search(p2, composed.rendered_text):
            r1 = layer_ranks.get(l1, 0)
            r2 = layer_ranks.get(l2, 0)
            
            winner_pattern = p1 if r1 > r2 else p2
            loser_pattern = p2 if r1 > r2 else p1
            winner_layer = l1 if r1 > r2 else l2
            loser_layer = l2 if r1 > r2 else l1
            
            conflicts_logged.append(f"Conflict resolved: {winner_layer} overrides {loser_layer}. Scrubbed '{loser_pattern}'")
            
            # Remove the loser pattern from all applicable packets (unless packet is HARD)
            for packet in composed.packets:
                if packet.constraint_class != "HARD":
                    packet.text = re.sub(loser_pattern, "", packet.text)
                    
    # Re-render after conflict resolution
    composed.rendered_text = "\n\n---\n\n".join(p.text.strip() for p in composed.packets if p.text.strip())
    composed.manifest["conflicts_resolved"] = conflicts_logged
    
    return composed
```

```python
def calibrate_coherence_thresholds(log_file_path: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Computes the optimal coherence threshold where findings/1k tokens drop by >10%."""
    import json
    from collections import defaultdict
    
    # Data structure: model -> density_bucket -> list of finding_rates
    data = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    
    with open(log_file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        for line in f:
            if not line.strip(): continue
            row = json.loads(line)
            
            model = row["model"]
            chars = row.get("directive_chars", 1)
            tokens = max(row.get("token_usage", len(row.get("response", "")) // 4), 1)
            constraints = row.get("constraint_count", 0)
            findings = row.get("findings_count", 0)
            
            density = constraints / max(chars // 4, 1)
            bucket = round(density, 3)
            rate_per_1k = findings / (tokens / 1000.0)
            
            data[model][bucket].append(rate_per_1k)
            
    optimal_thresholds = {}
    for model, buckets in data.items():
        # Calculate average rate per density bucket
        avg_rates = {b: sum(rates)/len(rates) for b, rates in buckets.items() if rates}
        if not avg_rates:
            continue
            
        sorted_buckets = sorted(avg_rates.keys())
        peak_density = max(avg_rates, key=avg_rates.get)
        peak_rate = avg_rates[peak_density]
        
        # Scan upwards from the peak density to find the 10% drop-off
        threshold = peak_density
        for b in sorted_buckets:
            if b > peak_density:
                if avg_rates[b] < (peak_rate * 0.90):
                    threshold = b
                    break
                    
        optimal_thresholds[model] = threshold
        
    return optimal_thresholds
```
